items.title: How to Spot a Blown Head Gasket
items.description: Early identification stops thermal warpage from destroying the cylinder head. Check these primary warning signs:

rows: Coolant loss, combustion gases entering cooling system

cards.title: What the symptoms mean
cards.text: Overheating: The head gasket has failed, allowing combustion gases to enter the cooling system. White smoke: Coolant is being drawn into the combustion chamber and burned. Mayonnaise: Coolant mixing with oil - a sure sign of head gasket failure. Coolant loss: Coolant is being burned in the combustion chamber. Misfire: Coolant in the cylinder disrupts combustion.

cards.title: ⚠️ The ticking clock
cards.text: A blown head gasket is a ticking time bomb . Continuing to drive will: 1. Warp the cylinder head - requiring machining/skimming. 2. Crack the cylinder head - requiring expensive replacement. 3. Damage the engine block - requiring block surfacing. 4. Destroy the engine - complete replacement required.

items.title: What It Is and Why It's Essential
items.description: What is head skimming? The cylinder head is machined on a precision surface grinder to remove micro-warping. This ensures a 100% gas-tight flat plane for the new multi-layer steel gasket to compress against.

rows: Almost always — overheating causes localized thermal warping
If warpage exceeds 0.5mm or if the casting has through-cracks

cards.title: Why skimming is essential
cards.text: The new gasket cannot seal correctly against an uneven, warped surface. The repair will fail again — often within a few hundred miles. Skipping skimming usually means paying for the entire labour job twice.

cards.title: Skimming limit
cards.text: Manufacturers specify a maximum skimming tolerance (typically 0.2mm to 0.5mm). If warpage exceeds this tolerance, skimming would reduce combustion chamber volume excessively, requiring head replacement.

items.title: What's the Most Common Cause of Head Gasket Failure?
items.description: Understanding why head gaskets fail allows you to prevent repeat failure after repair.

cards.title: The Top Causes
cards.text: Overheating - the primary culprit (60%+ of failures). Poor maintenance - degraded coolant, neglected flushing. Age and wear - thermal fatigue over 100k+ miles. Design issues - known head thermal stress points. Turbo issues - localized heat spikes and boost pressure. Head bolt failure - stretched or improperly torqued bolts.

cards.title: Why Overheating Causes Failure
cards.text: Aluminium cylinder head expands faster than iron or alloy block. Differential thermal expansion crushes and shears the gasket fire ring. Coolant channels and combustion chambers breach. Warping increases with every overheating cycle.

items.title: Common Questions About Head Gasket Repair
items.description: Everything you need to know about symptoms, repair costs, machine shop skimming, and warranties.

blocks.question: How much does head gasket repair cost in the UK? +
blocks.answer: Head gasket repair costs range from £550 to £2,000+ , with most drivers paying £700–£1,200 depending on vehicle type and engine layout. Small cars cost £465–£800, family cars £800–£1,200, SUVs £1,200–£1,850, and premium/luxury vehicles £1,500–£2,500+. Ignoring a blown head gasket leads to catastrophic engine damage and replacement costs of £2,000–£5,000+.

blocks.question: How do I know if my head gasket has blown? +
blocks.answer: Look for these signs: overheating, white smoke from exhaust, creamy "mayonnaise" under oil cap, coolant loss (no visible leak), misfire / rough running, bubbles in coolant reservoir, engine management light, loss of power, and oil in coolant. Overheating and white smoke are the most common signs.

blocks.question: Can I drive with a blown head gasket? +
blocks.answer: No — you should stop driving immediately. Continuing to drive will warp the cylinder head, crack the block, and destroy the engine. The cost of repair will escalate from £550–£1,200 to £2,000–£5,000+ for complete engine replacement.

blocks.question: What's included in head gasket repair? +
blocks.answer: Head gasket set, cylinder head skimming (if required), labour (8–15 hours), coolant refill, oil and filter change, and compression testing. Additional work (timing belt, water pump, etc.) is typically extra.

blocks.question: How long does head gasket repair take? +
blocks.answer: Typical repair time is 2–5 days . 4-cylinder engines take 2–4 days. V6/V8 engines take 3–5 days. The timeline depends on vehicle complexity, machine shop backlog for skimming, and parts availability.

blocks.question: Is it worth repairing a head gasket on an old car? +
blocks.answer: If the car is worth £2,000+ and otherwise in good condition, it's usually worth repairing. If the car is worth under £2,000, consider whether repair is economically viable. If the engine block is damaged, replacement engines cost £2,000–£5,000+.

blocks.question: What's the most common cause of head gasket failure? +
blocks.answer: Overheating is the most common cause (60%+ of failures). Other causes include poor maintenance (infrequent coolant changes), age and wear, cooling fan failures, stuck thermostats, turbo failure, and head bolt fatigue.

blocks.question: Should I replace the head gasket or the engine? +
blocks.answer: If the head gasket has blown but the cylinder head and block are structurally intact, repair with skimming is viable. If the head is cracked or the block cylinder liners are scored, engine replacement is more economical.

blocks.question: Can I repair a head gasket myself? +
blocks.answer: Head gasket replacement is not a DIY job for most owners. It requires precision timing locking tools, torque angle gauges, machine shop skimming equipment, and strict bolt torquing sequences. Use a professional specialist.

blocks.question: What's the labour time for head gasket repair? +
blocks.answer: 4-cylinder FWD: 8–12 hours. 4-cylinder RWD: 10–14 hours. V6: 12–16 hours. V8: 16–24 hours. Labour time depends on engine configuration and engine bay access.

blocks.question: How long does a head gasket repair last? +
blocks.answer: A properly repaired head gasket will last 100,000+ miles if the head was properly skimmed, new stretch bolts were used, and the cooling system is maintained with fresh antifreeze.

blocks.question: What happens if I ignore a blown head gasket? +
blocks.answer: The cylinder head will warp, crack, and potentially cause hydraulic lock (bent connecting rods). Repair costs quickly escalate from £550–£1,200 to £2,000–£5,000+ for complete engine replacement.

blocks.question: Does head gasket repair include the timing belt/chain? +
blocks.answer: Parts are charged extra, but there is no extra labour fee because the timing components are already removed during head disassembly. We strongly recommend renewing the timing kit and water pump at the same time.

blocks.question: Does head gasket repair affect insurance? +
blocks.answer: Standard OE repairs do not affect vehicle power or insurance category and do not require modification declaration. Keep invoice paperwork for full service history valuation.

mainEntity.name: How much does head gasket repair cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: Head gasket repair costs range from £550 to £2,000+, with most drivers paying £700-£1,200 depending on vehicle type and engine layout. Small cars cost £465-£800, family cars £800-£1,200, SUVs £1,200-£1,850, and premium/luxury vehicles £1,500-£2,500+. Ignoring a blown head gasket leads to catastrophic engine damage and replacement costs of £2,000-£5,000+.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my head gasket has blown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include engine overheating, thick white smoke from the exhaust, creamy 'mayonnaise' residue under the oil cap, unexplainable coolant loss, bubbling in the expansion tank, cylinder misfires, engine management lights, and loss of compression power.

mainEntity.name: Can I drive with a blown head gasket?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — you should stop driving immediately. Continuing to drive will warp the cylinder head, cause thermal cracking, score cylinder bores, and cause total engine seizure. A £700 repair can quickly escalate into a £3,500+ engine replacement.

mainEntity.name: What's included in head gasket repair?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard professional repair includes the multi-layer steel (MLS) head gasket set, new cylinder head stretch bolts, head surface skimming and pressure testing, 8-15 hours of labour, fresh coolant, engine oil, and an oil filter change.

mainEntity.name: How long does head gasket repair take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Typical workshop turnaround is 2 to 5 working days. A 4-cylinder inline engine takes 8-14 labour hours, whereas V6 and V8 engines take 14-24 hours due to twin cylinder bank dismantling and machining.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth repairing a head gasket on an old car?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the vehicle is worth £2,000+ and in solid overall mechanical condition, repairing the head gasket is usually worthwhile. If the repair cost exceeds 50-60% of the vehicle's market value, scrapping or selling for spares should be evaluated.

mainEntity.name: What's the most common cause of head gasket failure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Thermal overheating accounts for over 60% of failures. This is commonly triggered by coolant leaks, failed water pumps, stuck thermostats, faulty radiator fans, or degraded coolant. Age, high mileage, and localized cylinder head hot spots also contribute.

mainEntity.name: Should I replace the head gasket or the entire engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the cylinder head and block deck are structurally sound with no deep cracks, a head gasket replacement with skimming is the best path. If the head is cracked through the valve seats or the engine block itself is warped/scored, a reconditioned replacement engine is more reliable and cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: Can I repair a head gasket myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: Head gasket replacement is an advanced mechanical procedure requiring specialist timing locking tools, torque angle gauges, surface flatness micrometers, and precision machining equipment. DIY attempts without proper skimming frequently fail within weeks.

mainEntity.name: What's the labour time for head gasket repair?

acceptedAnswer.text: Labour time: 4-cylinder FWD requires 8-12 hours; 4-cylinder RWD requires 10-14 hours; V6 engines require 12-18 hours; V8 engines require 16-24 hours.

mainEntity.name: How long does a head gasket repair last?

acceptedAnswer.text: A properly skimmed cylinder head fitted with high-quality OEM or Victor Reinz MLS gaskets and new stretch bolts will comfortably last 100,000+ miles provided the cooling system is correctly maintained.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I ignore a blown head gasket?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ignoring symptoms leads through 5 progressive stages of damage: head warpage, head cracking, cylinder block distortion, hydraulic lock (bent connecting rods), and catastrophic engine destruction.

mainEntity.name: Does head gasket repair include the timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: Parts are usually charged extra, but because the timing belt/chain must already be removed to take the head off, there is zero additional labour cost. Specialists strongly recommend fitting a new timing kit and water pump simultaneously.

mainEntity.name: Does head gasket repair affect insurance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard OE-specification repairs do not alter performance or vehicle classification and do not need to be declared as modifications. Retaining garage invoices helps protect your car's resale value and provenance.
